blocks.text: Condo buildings in Granville
FORM by Anthem — 1530 West 6th Avenue

Current listings name the building "FORM by Anthem," place it in Fairview VW / South Granville, and record year built 2026, Apartment/Condo, with cats OK in the listing pet field. Unit count and full published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked. As a 2026 building, early sales carry new-build GST.
Pintura — 1530 West 8th Avenue

Listing copy describes "PINTURA, a boutique concrete building by Intracorp" in South Granville/Fairview; a listing records year built 2005, Apartment/Condo, concrete construction, and describes the building as "rental and pet friendly." A townhouse component also carries the Pintura name at 1576 West 8th Avenue (see the townhome subsection). Unit count: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
The Avedon — 1468 West 14th Avenue

A listing names the building "the AVEDON," records Property Type Apartment/Condo, year built 2007, concrete construction, zoning RM-3 and Title "Freehold Strata." Unit count and published rental/pet/age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
Landmark Sunset — 1412 West 14th Avenue

Listing copy names the building "Landmark Sunset" in Fairview, close to the South Granville shops; one listing records year built 1976 and frame-wood/stucco construction, while a building directory says it was built in 1978 and states its strata bylaws include "Pets allowed, rentals allowed" — the year conflict (1976 vs 1978) is flagged, not resolved, and a current listing adds that pets are allowed "but no more than two." Unit count: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
Streets, schools and getting around Granville

items.t: South Granville is a recognised smaller area of the city but not one of the City's 22 distinct local areas; the corridor runs through the Fairview local area, with the Shaughnessy local area at its south end. The South Granville Business Improvement Association district runs along Granville Street from the Granville Bridge to 16th Avenue; the residential side streets run east toward Oak Street and west toward Burrard Street. Exact board boundary roads: UNVERIFIED.

Where condo stock actually concentrates: on the residential side streets west and east of Granville — West 6th, West 8th and West 14th Avenues in the blocks between Burrard/Fir and Oak — not on the Granville Street retail frontage itself. The same side streets also hold the corridor's large stock of purpose-built rental apartment buildings, which is the defining trap of this area: many "apartment buildings" here are not condos at all.

Landmarks and retail: Gallery Row (the art-gallery stretch of the South Granville shopping district), the Stanley Theatre at 2750 Granville Street (650 seats, opened 1931 as a cinema and vaudeville house), Granville Park at 3001 Fir Street, and Vancouver General Hospital at 899 West 12th Avenue a few blocks east.

Transit: the corridor is bus-served today, including the 99 B-Line on West Broadway; the Broadway Subway — the 5.7 km Millennium Line extension with six underground stations including South Granville Station — is scheduled to enter service in fall 2027.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Granville

items.t: Area plan — the Broadway Plan: the Plan covers Clark Drive to Vine Street and 1st to 16th Avenues, was approved June 22, 2022 and updated in December 2024, and provides for a South Granville Station area with buildings up to 30–40 storeys near the station (40-storey maximum in the Granville/Burrard Slopes – Area A policy). Every building sits inside the Plan area — but the Plan is policy, not zoning: most higher-density forms still require rezoning. Citywide direction otherwise comes from the Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026.

City tax timing: Vancouver 2026 advance taxes were due February 3, 2026 and main taxes July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance after each due date; the home owner grant was also due July 3, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about Granville

items.t: The corridor's densest-looking blocks are its least buyable. The South Granville Apartment District — roughly West 11th to West 16th Avenues, Fir to Birch — is one of the city's only intact pre-WWII apartment neighbourhoods, held as rental assets; the strata stock sits on the quieter avenues north and south of it.
It was counted under Fairview in the earlier program; a buyer cross-shopping both areas will meet it there, not here, so totals across the two files do not double count it.
The station is dated, not rumoured.

Pintura is two products under one name. The West 8th Avenue development carries both apartment condos (1530 West 8th Avenue) and concrete townhouses (1576 West 8th Avenue) — a "Pintura" listing must be matched by address and type before it is compared.

The heritage apartment buildings carry two addresses each. Douglas Lodge is both 1507–1509 West 12th Avenue and 2799 Granville Street; Crescent Court is both 1504–1512 West 14th Avenue and 3003–3007 Granville Street — a search on one address alone gives a half picture of the same building.

The hospital is the corridor's quiet anchor tenant. Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue — BC's referral centre for many provincial programs and a teaching hospital — sits a few blocks east of Granville Street, which is a structural source of both owner and renter demand on the side streets.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Granville
Streets, schools and getting around Granville

items.t: Where the townhouse stock concentrates: on the residential side streets off Granville — West 6th, West 8th and West 14th Avenues in the blocks between Burrard/Fir and Oak — not on the Granville Street retail frontage itself. The corridor's one verified named townhouse complex (Pintura's townhouse component) sits on West 8th Avenue; the same side streets also hold unnamed strata townhouse addresses (documented, not counted) and the corridor's large stock of purpose-built rental apartment buildings, which is the defining trap of this area: many "apartment buildings" here are not strata at all.

Schools: SD39 catchments are address-based and checked in the VSB School Locator; SD39 has no middle-school tier (K–7 / 8–12). The catchment result for that sample address is UNVERIFIED — the locator was not run.

Market figures: Vancouver is outside SnapStats coverage in Jared's reports — the SnapStats FVR and GVR September 2026 reports contain no Vancouver community or sub-area rows — so no inventory, solds, sales-ratio, median-price, $/sqft, sale-to-list or days-on-market figure is published here for Granville / South Granville. All market figures for this area: UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Granville

items.t: Form B diligence (the Pintura townhouses, and any corridor strata purchase): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. In this corridor the Form B is also the fastest way to prove a building is a strata at all — the rental towers in have no Form B to give. Listing-level rental/pet lines in are listing data, not bylaws.

Fee-simple side-street houses: NO strata, NO Form B, NO strata fees — diligence is title, municipal rules (Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575) and any registered covenants or heritage designations only, stated plainly. The Heritage project's three houses are designated protected heritage property — heritage rules ride on top of whichever tenure title shows.

SSMUH / suite rules as the city states them: the R1-1 regime above is Vancouver's small-scale multi-unit housing frame — the suite and laneway permissions and the 6-unit / 8-rental-unit multiplex ceilings are what price the side-street lots around the corridor's strata stock.

Plan — the Broadway Plan: the Plan covers Clark Drive to Vine Street and 1st to 16th Avenues, was approved by Council on June 22, 2022 and updated in December 2024, and provides for a South Granville Station area with buildings up to 30–40 storeys near the station (40-storey maximum in the Granville/Burrard Slopes – Area A station-area policy). Every address sits inside the Plan area — but the Plan is policy, not zoning: most higher-density forms still require rezoning, and purpose-built rental buildings in the corridor carry tenant-relocation implications under the Plan's renter protections. Citywide direction otherwise comes from the Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about Granville

items.t: The board's "South Granville" label reaches far past South Granville. MLS files addresses as far south as 6160 Granville Street and 7128 Adera Street (Kerrisdale) under "South Granville" — a portal search on the sub-area name alone imports a different neighbourhood's stock into this corridor's results.

The station is dated, not rumoured. The Broadway Subway's South Granville Station is scheduled to enter service in fall 2027 on the Province's published date — corridor pricing already trades on that date, so a buyer should underwrite to it rather than to "someday."

Fairview was named in 1886 by CPR Land Commissioner L.A. Hamilton, whose survey established the numbered east–west avenues and named the cross streets after trees — which is why the corridor's townhouse addresses read as tree names (Fir, Birch, Hemlock) between Granville and Oak. Less than 100 years ago the False Creek and Fairview Slopes area was a forest of huge fir trees.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Granville
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Side-street house lots: detached houses and character homes on the quieter side streets of Fairview and the upper Shaughnessy edge, with low-rise and mid-rise condo and rental apartment buildings lining Granville Street and West Broadway. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees. The strata-versus-freehold split by street: UNVERIFIED.

Lot character, as the research states it: side-street house lots are governed by the R1-1 schedule where it applies (minimum site areas from 306 m² by form — 306 m² for a single detached house or duplex and for a multiple dwelling of 3 to 4 units, 464 m² for 5 units, 557 m² for 6 to 8 units); By-law No. 13817 amended the Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 to replace the old RS districts with R1-1, allowing up to 6 strata units, or up to 8 secured rental units, on former single-family lots, subject to the district schedule's site standards. The Granville Street frontage itself sits under commercial / mixed-use districts; the exact schedule for a given frontage parcel: UNVERIFIED. Parcel-level zone: UNVERIFIED.
Serviced position: corridor homes are on City water and sewer services; a 2026 utility dollar figure confirmed on a City source: UNVERIFIED.

ALR vs non-ALR: ALR land inside the corridor: UNVERIFIED in the research — no ALR parcel is confirmed and no split is stated. Flood position: the corridor's north end sits above the False Creek shoreline; whether a specific parcel is in the City's designated floodplain: UNVERIFIED.

Historic subdivisions = built lot fabric, not offerings: Fairview was named in 1886 by CPR Land Commissioner L.A. Hamilton, whose survey established the numbered east–west avenues and named the cross streets after trees — the side-street lot fabric is that historic survey, fully built, not an offering.

blocks.text: Bare-land strata

items.t: No bare-land strata plan or community in South Granville was verified: Stated plainly: a bare-land strata lot, wherever it exists in BC, IS strata tenure (Form B / strata fees / bylaws apply —); no such plan is documented for this ground.

blocks.text: Plan ground

items.t: Broadway Plan station ground: the Broadway Plan covers Clark Drive to Vine Street and 1st to 16th Avenues (approved June 22, 2022; updated December 2024) and provides for a South Granville Station area with buildings up to 30–40 storeys near the station — a 40-storey maximum in the Granville/Burrard Slopes – Area A station-area policy. The Plan is a policy framework, not a rezoning: most higher-density forms still require rezoning, and purpose-built rental buildings in the corridor carry tenant-relocation implications under the Plan's renter protections. No lot is presented as rezoned, assembled or for sale on this basis.
VGH campus ground: the Vancouver General Hospital campus east of the corridor is in a long-term redevelopment program — a documented redevelopment fact, not a land offering.

Board-filing trap — southern "South Granville" addresses are not this ground: MLS also files listings under a "South Granville" sub-area far south of this corridor — for example a listing at 519 7128 Adera Street (Kerrisdale) and a townhouse at 6160 Granville Street.
: No presale lot program was verified on a developer or government source.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Granville

items.t: Nearby areas: Fairview (the surrounding local area), Kitsilano across the Granville Bridge side via West Broadway, Shaughnessy to the south, Arbutus Ridge to the south-west, and downtown Vancouver across False Creek.

Where land interest concentrates: on the residential side streets west and east of Granville — West 6th, West 8th and West 14th Avenues in the blocks between Burrard/Fir and Oak — and on the Granville / Broadway station ground. The Granville Street retail frontage itself sits under commercial / mixed-use districts. The same side streets hold the corridor's large stock of purpose-built rental apartment buildings — many "apartment buildings" here are not strata at all.

Transit: the corridor is bus-served today, including the 99 B-Line along West Broadway; the Broadway Subway — the 5.7 km Millennium Line extension with six new underground stations including South Granville Station — is scheduled to enter service in fall 2027. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.
Schools: SD39 catchments are address-based, with no middle-school tier (K–7 / 8–12). School names use Ministry-listed names only.
All market figures: UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Granville

items.t: Zoning — Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575, R1-1 (side streets, via By-law No. 13817) + commercial / mixed-use (frontage): R1-1 allows up to 6 strata units, or up to 8 secured rental units, on former single-family lots, subject to the district schedule (306 m² / 464 m² / 557 m² minimum site areas by form; secondary suite and laneway house with a house). The Granville Street frontage sits under commercial / mixed-use districts; a corridor strata example, The Avedon, is recorded in its listing as zoned RM-3. Exact schedule per frontage parcel: UNVERIFIED.

Plan — the Broadway Plan + Vancouver Official Development Plan: the Broadway Plan (Clark Drive to Vine Street, 1st to 16th Avenues; approved June 22, 2022; updated December 2024) sets the station-area heights in — policy, not zoning. Citywide direction otherwise comes from the Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026. Distinguish plan policy from zoning before pricing any corridor lot on tower density.

Subdivision — Subdivision By-law No. 5208, fees by No. 14538: Vancouver subdivision is governed by the Subdivision By-law (No. 5208), whose Schedule A sets minimum parcel width and area standards by district and sub-area category, administered by the Approving Officer; its fee schedule was most recently amended for 2026 by By-law No. 14538 (enacted December 9, 2025, in force January 1, 2026). A fee-simple split of a side-street lot must clear both its district schedule and its Subdivision By-law category — neither is assumed from a neighbouring lot's history.

Heritage / character diligence (documented for this corridor): the three Sixteenth & Burrard houses are designated protected heritage property, and Douglas Lodge and Crescent Court sit on the City's Heritage Register — heritage rules ride on top of whichever tenure title shows, and character-home retention rules must be confirmed before marketing "development potential" on a side-street lot.

Strata diligence (the corridor's strata stock — and any bare-land strata lot, if one is ever met here): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page) — in this corridor the Form B is also the fastest way to prove a building is a strata at all, since the rental towers have no Form B to give; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children); a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no corridor ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

faq.q: Does the site's "Granville" area mean downtown Granville Street?
faq.a: No — for this page the ground is South Granville, the west-side corridor from the Granville Bridge to West 16th Avenue; the City lists "South Granville" as a recognised smaller area and places its Gallery Row shopping district inside Fairview.

faq.q: Is South Granville part of the Broadway Plan?
faq.a: Yes — the Broadway Plan covers Clark Drive to Vine Street and 1st to 16th Avenues and was approved June 22, 2022; it provides for a South Granville Station area with buildings up to 30–40 storeys near the station.

faq.q: When does the Broadway Subway reach South Granville?
faq.a: The 5.7 km Millennium Line extension, with six underground stations including South Granville Station, is scheduled to enter service in fall 2027.

faq.q: Can a side-street house lot be redeveloped as a multiplex?
faq.a: Generally yes where the R1-1 schedule is met — By-law No. 13817 allows up to 6 strata units (or 8 secured rental units) on former single-family lots, subject to the district schedule; heritage-designated properties carry additional rules.
The Stanley Theatre, 2750 Granville Street at West 12th Avenue — a 650-seat venue in a 1931 art deco building whose restoration received a 1999 City of Vancouver Heritage Award.
No. The downtown entertainment corridor is a different market and none of its buildings appear here.

faq.q: Why do so many South Granville "apartment buildings" never have units for sale?
faq.a: Because they are purpose-built rentals held as whole assets: The Leeward is a 48-suite rental tower (1968) and Santa Monica a 13-suite rental building (1929), and the West 11th–16th / Fir–Birch district is documented as an intact pre-WWII rental apartment neighbourhood. A building name on the Heritage Register (Douglas Lodge, Crescent Court) is not evidence of strata tenure.

faq.q: Can I rent out a corridor condo long-term?
faq.a: Yes — rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022; Pintura is described in listings as rental-friendly and Landmark Sunset's directory entry says rentals allowed. Short-term rentals can still be restricted, and the Empty Homes Tax declaration applies to a unit left empty.

faq.q: When does the SkyTrain reach South Granville, and does the Broadway Plan change my building?
faq.a: South Granville Station is one of six underground stations on the Broadway Subway, scheduled to enter service in fall 2027. The Broadway Plan (1st–16th, Vine to Clark) contemplates 30–40 storeys near the station, which changes land-value assumptions block by block — but the Plan is policy, not zoning, and most tower forms still need rezoning.
Sources conflict: a listing says 1976, a building directory says 1978. flags both; the strata plan registration record is the definitive check.
No. The downtown entertainment corridor is a different market and none of its buildings appear here.

faq.a: One verified named complex: the Pintura townhouses at 1576 West 8th Avenue (concrete, built 2005, part of the Intracorp Pintura strata whose apartments sit at 1530 West 8th Avenue).
